name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before human review. It catches style, docs, and simple logic errors early, freeing humans to focus on design and edge cases. The trade-off is slower initial feedback for contributors—PR-Agent adds 30-60 seconds per PR—but the net time saved in later review rounds outweighs it.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 30-60s delay isn’t the real cost—it’s the false positives drowning design reviews in noise. A better alternative is to run PR-Agent only after human triage flags a PR as high-risk, cutting wasted time. Settle it by measuring how many PR-Agent comments actually change the final diff versus how many get ignored.
